title: One number and a list of turnings

data.source: Invariance of arc length under reparametrisation; Chentsov (1972); Amari's alpha-connections (1985). Numerical check on the worked circle of Phoenix_Egg/CORE/MATHEMATICS.md, the lens's generic circle and test path, and 30 more random paths and 30 more random circles, seeded.

prediction: Changing the clock leaves the cuts, C and B alone (G1); the turning values alone give the same cuts and C (G2); reversing the direction or the time changes the cut count though the path length is the same (G3); and the circle's length survives relabelling and outcome splitting but not merging (G4).
baseline: Reparametrisation invariance of arc length, Chentsov's theorem and Amari's alpha-connections; and a decoy ruler, the plain Euclidean length of the curve of probabilities.
why: All four statements held and all four are textbook: arc length ignores the clock and the labels, the Fisher ruler ignores a fixed splitting of outcomes (Chentsov), and a first-passage count needs a direction. CRR adds no prediction here. What the check makes plain is how little is fixed: one number for the circle, and a list of turning heights for the path.

alternatives.null_worlds: 30 random paths: G1 held on 30, G2 on 29. 30 random circles: G4 held on 30, the variant's statements on 30, the decoy ruler was fooled on 30.

operating_characteristics: Identity room: every statement is a theorem or its numerical echo, so no outcome weighs for or against CRR as a claim about the world.
second_check: Adapted and re-run by a worker who did not write the mapping. No person has reviewed it.
variants: V-mathematical-2 (the skewness circulation h; museum experiment, not the owner's CRR)
